{{Short description|Special function defined by a Gaussian integral}}

In mathematics, the '''Goodwin–Staton integral''' is the [[special function]]
<ref name="DLMF-def">{{cite web
 |title=DLMF §7.2(v), Goodwin–Staton Integral
 |url=https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.2#E12
 |work=NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
 |publisher=[[National Institute of Standards and Technology]]
 |access-date=9 August 2026
}}</ref>
:<math>G(z)=\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t^2}}{t+z}\,dt,\qquad |\arg z|<\pi.</math>

The restriction on the argument excludes the non-positive real axis, where the denominator can vanish along the path of integration. The integral is named after E. T. Goodwin and J. Staton, who published a numerical table of the corresponding real integral in 1948.<ref name="GoodwinStaton">{{cite journal
 |last1=Goodwin
 |first1=E. T.
 |last2=Staton
 |first2=J.
 |title=Table of f(x)=∫₀^∞ e^(−u²)/(u+x) du
 |journal=[[The Quarterly Journal of Mechanics and Applied Mathematics]]
 |volume=1
 |issue=1
 |year=1948
 |pages=319–326
 |doi=10.1093/qjmam/1.1.319
}}</ref>

== Relation to other special functions ==

For positive real <math>x</math>, the Goodwin–Staton integral is related to [[Dawson function|Dawson's integral]] <math>F</math> and the [[exponential integral]] by<ref name="DLMF-rel">{{cite web
 |title=DLMF §7.5, equation 7.5.13
 |url=https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.5#E13
 |work=NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
 |publisher=[[National Institute of Standards and Technology]]
 |access-date=9 August 2026
}}</ref>
:<math>G(x)=\sqrt{\pi}\,F(x)-\frac12 e^{-x^2}\mathrm{Ei}(x^2),\qquad x>0.</math>

== Differential equations ==

Differentiating the defining integral and integrating by parts gives the first-order inhomogeneous differential equation
:<math>G'(z)+2zG(z)=\sqrt{\pi}-\frac1z.</math>

Differentiating this relation twice and eliminating the inhomogeneous term gives the third-order linear homogeneous equation
:<math>zG'''(z)+(2+2z^2)G''(z)+8zG'(z)+4G(z)=0.</math>

== Properties on the positive real axis ==

For <math>x>0</math>, differentiation under the integral sign gives
:<math>G^{(n)}(x)=(-1)^n n!\int_0^\infty \frac{e^{-t^2}}{(t+x)^{n+1}}\,dt.</math>

Hence
:<math>(-1)^nG^{(n)}(x)>0,\qquad n=0,1,2,\ldots,</math>
so <math>G</math> is a [[completely monotonic function]] on <math>(0,\infty)</math>. In particular, <math>G</math> is positive, strictly decreasing, and convex there.

== Series near the origin ==

D. S. Jones studied the generalized Goodwin–Staton integral and obtained convergent series representations.<ref name="Jones">{{cite journal
 |last=Jones
 |first=D. S.
 |title=The generalized Goodwin–Staton integral
 |journal=Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society
 |volume=48
 |issue=3
 |year=2005
 |pages=635–650
 |doi=10.1017/S0013091504001087
}}</ref> Specializing Jones's equation (2.11) gives, for <math>|\arg z|<\pi</math>,
:<math>G(z)=e^{-z^2}\left(-\log z-\frac{\gamma}{2}-\frac12\sum_{m=1}^{\infty}\frac{z^{2m}}{m!\,m}+\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac{z^{2m+1}}{m!\left(m+\frac12\right)}\right),</math>
where <math>\log z</math> is the principal logarithm and <math>\gamma</math> is the [[Euler–Mascheroni constant]].

Consequently, as <math>z\to0</math> within the cut plane,
:<math>G(z)=-\log z-\frac{\gamma}{2}+\sqrt{\pi}\,z+\left(\log z+\frac{\gamma}{2}-\frac12\right)z^2-\frac{2\sqrt{\pi}}{3}z^3+\left(\frac38-\frac{\gamma}{4}-\frac12\log z\right)z^4+O(z^5).</math>

In particular,
:<math>G(x)\sim-\log x-\frac{\gamma}{2}\qquad (x\to0^+).</math>

== Asymptotic expansion ==

For large positive <math>x</math>, the integral has the asymptotic expansion<ref name="Jones" />
:<math>G(x)\sim\frac12\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(-1)^n\Gamma\left(\frac{n+1}{2}\right)x^{-n-1}\qquad (x\to+\infty).</math>

Thus its first terms are
:<math>G(x)\sim\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2x}-\frac{1}{2x^2}+\frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{4x^3}-\frac{1}{2x^4}+\frac{3\sqrt{\pi}}{8x^5}-\frac{1}{x^6}+\cdots.</math>

The [[NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions]] refers to Olver for corresponding expansions with bounds on the remainder for both real and complex values of the argument.<ref name="DLMF-asymp">{{cite web
 |title=DLMF §7.12(iii), Goodwin–Staton Integral
 |url=https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.12#iii
 |work=NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
 |publisher=[[National Institute of Standards and Technology]]
 |access-date=9 August 2026
}}</ref>

== Generalized Goodwin–Staton integral ==

Jones considered the generalized integral<ref name="Jones" />
:<math>I(\mu,z)=\int_0^\infty \frac{t^\mu e^{-t^2}}{t-z}\,dt,</math>
where <math>\mu</math> is real with <math>\mu>-1</math> and <math>z</math> lies off the positive real axis. The ordinary Goodwin–Staton integral is the special case
:<math>G(z)=I(0,-z).</math>

The generalized integral is a [[Stieltjes transformation|Stieltjes transform]] and satisfies the recurrence
:<math>I(\mu+1,z)=\frac12\Gamma\left(\frac{\mu+1}{2}\right)+zI(\mu,z),</math>
as well as
:<math>\frac{\partial I(\mu,z)}{\partial z}=\mu I(\mu-1,z)-2I(\mu+1,z),\qquad \mu>0.</math>

Jones derived convergent series, asymptotic expansions, and explicit error bounds, and also treated oscillatory and logarithmic variants.<ref name="Jones" /> Mamedov later gave another evaluation of generalized Goodwin–Staton integrals using the binomial expansion theorem.<ref name="Mamedov">{{cite journal
 |last=Mamedov
 |first=B. A.
 |title=Evaluation of the generalized Goodwin–Staton integral using binomial expansion theorem
 |journal=Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer
 |volume=105
 |issue=1
 |year=2007
 |pages=8–11
 |doi=10.1016/j.jqsrt.2006.09.018
}}</ref>

== Numerical evaluation ==

For positive real arguments, numerical evaluation can be reduced to Dawson's integral and the exponential integral through the relation above.<ref name="DLMF-rel" /> For small and moderate arguments, Jones's convergent series can be used, while for large arguments the asymptotic expansion is more suitable.<ref name="Jones" /> The DLMF section on computation of the Goodwin–Staton integral cites the original table of Goodwin and Staton.<ref name="DLMF-comp">{{cite web
 |title=DLMF §7.22(ii), Goodwin–Staton Integral
 |url=https://dlmf.nist.gov/7.22#ii
 |work=NIST Digital Library of Mathematical Functions
 |publisher=[[National Institute of Standards and Technology]]
 |access-date=9 August 2026
}}</ref>
